The collection now has 7 numbered folders with 94 requests:

Folder	Requests	Covers
0 Setup	4	Creates Alice, Bob, T1 and a completed task T2done, and saves their ids
1 Create & validate	23	Every 400 and 404 case for POST, default values, dateCreated being ignored, an unknown route
2 select on single resources	8	select includes and excludes, where ignored on /:id, 404s for bad and nonexistent ids
3 Updating missing resources	6	PUT to nonexistent or malformed ids, which must return 404 even when the body is also invalid
4 Two-way references	19	Every row of the README and FAQ tables, plus failed requests followed by a GET to confirm nothing changed
5 Query parameters	19	where, $in, sort, skip/limit, count, combined parameters, invalid JSON
6 Deleting	12	Deleted tasks leave pendingTasks; deleting a user unassigns all their tasks, completed ones too; repeat deletes return 404
7 Teardown	3	Deletes the remaining test data
How it works:

Expected status comes from the request name. For example, User missing email → 400 expects a 400. A collection-level test checks that status on every request, along with the {message, data} shape and that no Mongoose error text leaks into the response.
The two-way reference tests check both sides. After each change, they fetch the task or user from the other side to confirm it was updated too.
No stray data is left behind. Some negative tests create a resource when they shouldn't, such as the name: 123 one; those resources are deleted automatically. So are resources from requests marked (temp).
Point it at your server with baseUrl. It's a collection variable, set to http://localhost:3000 for now. Change it to your Render URL to test the deployed API.
Expected failures: the 6 requests marked ⚠️ in their descriptions test the gaps from the code review: wrong types, malformed JSON, assignedUserName without assignedUser, the description default, limit with the wrong shape, and the HTML 404. They'll fail until those are fixed. The Mongoose-leak check will also fail on any GET that hits the CastError branch.

Run it with the folders in order: in Postman, open the collection and choose Run. Alternatively, start your server with npm start, log in to the Postman CLI with postman login, and I can run the collection from here and go through the failures with you.
